newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Chekiang First Bank seen in LAF-eligible FRCD.
newsitem.headline: HK's Chekiang First Bank seen in LAF-eligible FRCD.

text.p: Hong Kong-based Chekiang First Bank may launch a floating rate certificates of deposit issue before the end of March, market sources said.
The borrower is wholly-owned by Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank.
Bankers said the proposed issue would be HK$1.0 billion in size and carry a maturity of five years with put and call options in years three and four.
With fees, the all-in return will be in the mid-40s over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
The sources said they expect the bank to apply to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the issue as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
Chekiang First Bank is rated A-plus by IBCA.
Sources said Bayerische Landesbank, DKB Asia, HSBC Markets and Schroders Asia will arrange the deal. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6960
